en: In order to use Codex, no matter if you're
using the CLI or this desktop application,
you need a paid plan. Though, to be very
precise, right now when I'm recording this,
you can actually try it for free, but this
is only a temporary offer for the release of
the Codex desktop application. And in
general, you will want a paid plan to get
the most out of it. This is included with
your ChatGPT subscription if you already
have one. So if you're already paying for
ChatGPT, you can kind of use Codex for free
in addition to your existing subscription.
Now I'm using the Pro subscription here to
get the most out of Codex because I am
actively using it for all of my projects in
conjunction with Claude Code actually.
But you will get a decent amount of usage
already out of Codex by using Plus. And of
course there also are business and
enterprise plans you may be using as a
company. It's also worth noting though that
you can actually also use other providers.
You are actually not limited to the models
provided by OpenAI. So you could use the
Codex tools, at least right now when I'm
recording this,
without a subscription and without the
OpenAI models. But of course, no matter
which other models you might be using,
you'll probably have to pay for them, except
for
locally running models, of course, which you
can also use with Codex, which is something
I will also show you. But you have to be
aware of the fact that those models are not
nearly as capable as the Codex or the
Anthropic models. And therefore, in the end,
no matter how you will use Codex, you will
very likely need a paid plan.
